<reason>PRO won the central clash on whether engineering limits substitute for individualized judgment. A showed limits and screening address different risks, that labels concede suitability matters without solving self-identification and cumulative effects, and that commercial incentives plus distorted self-perception make brain stimulation distinct from whiskey/tanning beds. CON never proved reversibility or that DIY substitution outweighs mass-marketing expansion, and conceded screening benefit while reducing oversight to denial without answering continuing follow-up.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's complementary-protections reply - hardware ceiling constrains machine not person, prescribed home use works because screening plus bounds plus follow-up operate together, locked setting is not clinical judgment - which directly neutralized B's bounds-do-the-work claim.</best_rebuttal>
